mainTopic: שמואל's rulings on פסי ביראות, the משנה on carrying in an enclosed garden or קרפף, and the meaning of ״וְעוֹד״
overview: The amud opens with two rulings of שמואל about פסי ביראות. First, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא, so the boards are allowed only for a public well. Second, they are allowed only for a well of מים חיים. Through a צריכותא, the גמרא shows that each ruling adds its own condition, so the well must be both public and spring-fed. Next comes a new משנה about carrying in a walled גינה or קרפף of about seventy אמות square. רבי יהודה בן בבא requires a sign of living there, רבי יהודה accepts a water feature, and רבי עקיבא requires nothing beyond the size limit. רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי then argue about whether the area must be square. רבי אלעאי reports three rulings he heard from his teacher, but no other student confirmed them. The גמרא then asks why the משנה says ״וְעוֹד״ and concludes that it fits only when the same תנא's statements are not broken up by an argument on a different topic. Finally, it quotes רבי עקיבא's view to open a new discussion.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יהודה בן בבא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יוסף said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ruling from שמואל. He says the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא, who held in the משנה that boards may be set up only for a public well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה בן בבא limited פסי ביראות to באר הרבים, a well used by the public. For any other well, he required a full ten-טפחים-high enclosure (חגורה). שמואל decides the law according to that limiting view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The practical law follows the view of...
The תנא who limits boards to a public well

phrases.english: Gemara

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava.
phrases.notes: His view is that boards are allowed only for a public well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא: פסי ביראות are allowed only for a public well.

steps.title: Boards are allowed only for a spring-water well
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a second ruling: פסי ביראות are allowed only for a well of מים חיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף also said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said: The boards around wells were permitted only for a well of fresh spring water.
steps.whatsHappening: The same chain of teachers reports a second ruling from שמואל. Boards around a well are allowed only if the well has living spring water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסי ביראות are a special leniency that lets people draw water on שבת. This ruling limits that leniency to מים חיים, water flowing from a spring. A pit of collected rainwater does not qualify. Now we have two rulings that both seem to limit the same leniency, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Upright boards set at the corners around a well to form an enclosure for שבת

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The boards of wells were not permitted
except for a well of spring water alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא הוּתְּרוּ פַּסֵּי בֵירָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same chain, placed right next to the first
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסי ביראות are allowed only for a well of מים חיים.

steps.title: Why the second ruling is needed: a public cistern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its צריכותא. If we had only the first ruling, we might allow boards for a public well even if it holds collected water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was necessary to say both. For if he had taught us only that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא, I would have said that for a public well, boards are allowed even if the water is collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל needed to say both rulings. It starts by showing what we would get wrong if we had only the first ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling only tells us the well must be public. From that alone, we might think any public well works, even a cistern of מכונסין. So the second ruling, which requires מים חיים, is needed to block that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was necessary to state both
If he had taught us only...
I would have thought (the mistaken first assumption)
Collected water, such as rainwater gathered in a cistern

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read וּצְרִיכָא as an argument against שמואל. It is a defense of his words: it shows that neither ruling is extra.

phrases.english: And it was necessary (to state both):
For if he had taught us
"the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava,"
I would have said:
for a public well, even collected water is fine,
phrases.notes: Only the public status would seem to matter, not the type of water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא: דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why both rulings are needed
steps.kashyaTarget: An unspoken question: the two rulings seem to repeat each other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the first ruling alone, a public well would qualify even with collected water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second ruling is needed to require מים חיים.

steps.title: The משנה's wording does not settle it, so שמואל had to say it
steps.stepSummary: The words באר הרבים in the משנה might seem to exclude cisterns. The גמרא explains that this wording was only meant to reject רבי עקיבא, so שמואל's second ruling is truly needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the משנה says 'a public well,' that was only to exclude the view of רבי עקיבא. So שמואל teaches us that boards were permitted only for a well of spring water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the mistaken 'I would have said' (הוה אמינא) from step 3. Without שמואל's second ruling, one would read the משנה's phrase באר הרבים as aimed only at rejecting רבי עקיבא, who allowed boards for a private well, and not as excluding a cistern. Then קא משמע לן: שמואל's second ruling teaches that only a well of מים חיים qualifies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might object that the משנה's word באר already rules out a cistern, which would make the second ruling unnecessary. The הוה אמינא answers that the whole phrase באר הרבים only contrasts public with private, against רבי עקיבא, so it says nothing about the type of water. That is why שמואל had to state the מים חיים requirement explicitly.

phrases.english: And this that the Mishnah teaches, "a public well" —
is to exclude the view of Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא allowed boards even for a private well.

phrases.english: So he teaches us
that the boards of wells were not permitted
except for a well of spring water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי דְּקָתָנֵי בְּאֵר הָרַבִּים — לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first half of the צריכותא by explaining away the משנה's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the purpose of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase באר הרבים only rejects רבי עקיבא's private well, so a public cistern of collected water would also qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: That phrase only excludes רבי עקיבא's private well, so the ruling on מים חיים is new.

steps.title: Why the first ruling is needed: a private spring well
steps.stepSummary: If we had only the ruling about מים חיים, we might allow boards even for a private spring well. So the first ruling is needed to require a public well.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only about a well of spring water, I would have said there is no difference between public and private. So he teaches us that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא from the other side. Without the first ruling, we might think any spring well works, even a private one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ruling looks only at the type of water. On its own, it would leave the door open for a יחיד's spring well. The first ruling closes that door. So each ruling covers a different condition, and both conditions are required.
steps.whatToRemember: Two conditions together: פסי ביראות are allowed only for a well that is both public (רבי יהודה בן בבא) and full of מים חיים. A public cistern fails, and so does a private spring well.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא treats two short rulings from the same sage. Each one adds its own condition, and together they define the exact limits of this שבת leniency.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only "a well of spring water,"
I would have said:
there is no difference whether it is public
and no difference whether it is private,
so he teaches us:
the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא itself repeats the first ruling, now to show why it is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּאֵר מַיִם חַיִּים, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: לָא שְׁנָא דְּרַבִּים וְלָא שְׁנָא דְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror-image half of the צריכותא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the second ruling alone, a private spring well would qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ruling requires that the well be public.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are needed. Boards are allowed only for a public well of spring water.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא: an enclosed garden needs a living element
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. רבי יהודה בן בבא says one may carry in an enclosed גינה or קרפף of about 70 by 70 אמות only if it has a watchman's booth, a house, or is near the town.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: And רבי יהודה בן בבא also said: a garden or a קרפף that is seventy אמות and a little more by seventy אמות and a little more, and is surrounded by a wall ten טפחים high, may be carried in. This is only allowed if it has a watchman's booth or a house in it, or if it is close to the town.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with another ruling of רבי יהודה בן בבא, this time about carrying inside a fenced-in garden or storage yard. He says the walls and the size are not enough. The place must also be connected to living in some way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An area fenced in for living, like a חצר, may be carried in at any size. An area fenced in for other uses, like a garden, has a size limit of בית סאתיים, which is the 70-and-a-bit-squared area. רבי יהודה בן בבא adds a further condition: the place also needs a sign that people use it like a home, such as a watchman's booth, a house, or being next to town.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed yard behind the houses, used for storage, and not fenced in for living
Seventy אמות and a little more, the side of a square equal to בית סאתיים (5,000 square אמות)
A dwelling, a house to live in

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole משנה. The question is what makes a non-living enclosure count as a place where carrying is allowed. רבי יהודה and רבי עקיבא then each become more lenient about this requirement, before the משנה turns to a separate argument about shape.

phrases.english: MISHNA

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא:
phrases.english: And furthermore Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava said:
phrases.notes: "Furthermore" links back to his earlier ruling in the previous משנה about פסי ביראות

phrases.english: A garden or a karpef
that are seventy cubits and a remainder
by seventy cubits and a remainder
that are surrounded by a wall ten handbreadths high
one may carry inside it,
provided that it has a watchman's booth in it
or a dwelling place,
or that it is near the town.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It continues with rulings of רבי יהודה בן בבא, whose earlier ruling שמואל adopted in steps 1-5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An enclosed גינה or קרפף of up to בית סאתיים may be carried in only if it has a watchman's booth, a house, or is near the town.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even a water feature is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is more lenient. Even a cistern, a ditch, or a cave in the garden is enough to permit carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even if it has only a cistern, a ditch, or a cave, one may carry inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי יהודה בן בבא and makes it easier. You do not need a house or a booth. A water source in the garden is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees that some living element is needed. However, he widens what counts. People come to use water, so a water feature also gives the place a 'used like a home' character.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern, a pit that holds water
A cave, here a covered pit holding water

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהודה (step 7) with רבי יהודה בן בבא (step 6). They are two different תנאים with different opinions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
even if it contains only
a cistern, a ditch, or a cave
one may carry inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 6 and lowers the requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cistern, ditch, or cave alone is enough to permit carrying in the enclosed garden.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: only the size limit matters
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says no living element is needed at all. Only the size limit of 70-and-a-bit by 70-and-a-bit counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: even if it has none of these things, one may carry inside it, as long as it is no bigger than seventy אמות and a little more by seventy אמות and a little more.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא is the most lenient so far. He says you need no house, booth, or water. The only rule is the size limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בבא and רבי יהודה both required some sign of living use. רבי עקיבא drops that requirement completely. For him, any walled area up to בית סאתיים is fine. This matches his lenient view in the earlier משנה about פסי ביראות.

keyTerms.meaning: Any one of all these things (booth, house, water feature)
Provided that, only on condition that

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אַחַת מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ
phrases.english: even if it has none of these
one may carry inside it,
provided that it measures

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִים עַל שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִים.
phrases.english: seventy cubits and a remainder by seventy cubits and a remainder.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אַחַת מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than step 7 and removes the living requirement entirely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any walled garden or קרפף up to בית סאתיים may be carried in, with no living element required.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: it must be a perfect square
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר turns to the shape of the area. If the length is longer than the width by even one אמה, carrying is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: if its length is more than its width, even by one אמה, one may not carry inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves from what must be inside the garden to what shape it must have. רבי אליעזר is very strict: the area must be a perfect square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the total area stays within בית סאתיים, רבי אליעזר forbids carrying when the shape is not square. For him, the size limit is measured as an exact square of 70-and-a-bit by 70-and-a-bit, so any stretching ruins it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיְתָה אׇרְכָּהּ יָתֵר עַל רׇחְבָּהּ
phrases.english: if its length was greater than its breadth
even by one cubit
one may not carry inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיְתָה אׇרְכָּהּ יָתֵר עַל רׇחְבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic within the משנה: the required shape of the enclosure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The enclosure must be exactly square. If it is longer than it is wide by even one אמה, carrying is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: even double length is fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי אליעזר. Even if the length is twice the width, carrying is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even if its length is double its width, one may carry inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues against רבי אליעזר about the shape. He says a rectangle is fine, even one twice as long as it is wide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the shape does not need to be square. A shape up to 2-to-1, like the 100-by-50 courtyard of the משכן, still works, as long as the total area stays within the limit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
even if its length is double its breadth
one may carry inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אׇרְכָּהּ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּרׇחְבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees directly with step 9 about the required shape.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An enclosure whose length is up to double its width may still be carried in.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי: a tradition allowing even a בית כור
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי reports that he heard from רבי אלעזר that carrying is allowed even in a garden as large as a בית כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי said: I heard from רבי אלעזר that one may carry even if the garden is as big as a בית כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a surprising tradition. רבי אלעאי reports that his teacher allowed carrying even in a huge area, a בית כור, which is far bigger than בית סאתיים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, every opinion kept the size limit of בית סאתיים. This report allows an area about fifteen times larger. That seems to clash with the size limit, and it is especially striking if it comes from the strict רבי אליעזר of step 9. The גמרא will need to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: An area that takes a כור of seed (75,000 square אמות), much larger than בית סאתיים

steps.confusionAlert: Our text reads רבי אלעזר, while some read 'רבי אליעזר'. Either way, the claim is surprising, because it goes far beyond the בית סאתיים limit that the rest of the משנה assumes.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two separate arguments. The first is about what must be inside the garden: רבי יהודה בן בבא requires a booth, a house, or closeness to town; רבי יהודה accepts a water feature; רבי עקיבא requires nothing. The second is about shape: רבי אליעזר requires a perfect square, and רבי יוסי allows up to 2-to-1. Finally, רבי אלעאי reports a tradition allowing even a בית כור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai said:
I heard from Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: Some versions read this name as רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: even if it is the size of a beit kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעַאי: שָׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a far more lenient tradition about size after the shape argument in steps 9-10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the tradition רבי אלעאי received, carrying is allowed even in an enclosed garden the size of a בית כור.

steps.title: A neighbor who forgot to join the courtyard עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי reports a second ruling from רבי אליעזר. If one resident of a חצר forgot to join the עירוב, only he is restricted. The others may still carry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also heard from him: if one of the residents of a חצר forgot and did not join the עירוב, he may not bring things into or out of his house. But the other residents are allowed to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעאי is still quoting things he heard from רבי אליעזר. This is a new ruling about a חצר עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, one neighbor who did not join the עירוב would stop everyone from carrying in the חצר. Here he gave up his share of the חצר to the others. So only he is blocked from carrying to and from his house. The others may carry, even into his house through the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: And I also heard from him: רבי אלעאי adding another report
The residents who share a courtyard
To bring in and to take out (to carry)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that one person forgetting the עירוב ruins it for everyone here. In this case, only the one who forgot is restricted.

phrases.english: And I also heard from him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעאי talking, and "him" is רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Residents of a courtyard
where one of them forgot and did not join the eruv —
his house is forbidden for him to bring in and take out,
but for them it is permitted.
phrases.notes: The other residents may still carry

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second report from the same source, רבי אליעזר. It moves from garden size to a courtyard עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The resident who forgot the עירוב may not carry to and from his house. The other residents may carry.

steps.title: ערקבלין can be used for מרור
steps.stepSummary: A third report from רבי אליעזר: one fulfills the מצוה of מרור on פסח with ערקבלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also heard from him that one fulfills his obligation on פסח with ערקבלין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעאי adds a third ruling he heard from רבי אליעזר, this time about פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling has nothing to do with carrying on שבת. It appears here only because רבי אלעאי heard it from the same teacher. ערקבלין is a type of bitter herb, and it counts as מרור.

phrases.english: And I also heard from him:
that one fulfills the obligation with arkablin on Passover.
phrases.notes: The obligation of bitter herbs

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third report in the same chain of rulings from רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: No other student heard these rulings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי says he asked all of רבי אליעזר's students. He could not find anyone else who heard these three rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: I went around to all of his students looking for a colleague who heard this too, and I did not find one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעאי closes his report. He admits that no one else confirmed these rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This remark covers all three rulings: the big garden, the forgotten עירוב, and ערקבלין. It tells us these traditions rest only on רבי אלעאי's testimony. It also closes the משנה before the גמרא begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A colleague (here, someone to back up the report)

steps.whatToRemember: The three rulings רבי אלעאי reports from רבי אליעזר are the בית כור garden, the forgotten עירוב, and ערקבלין. No other student confirmed them.

phrases.english: And I went around to all his students
and sought for myself a colleague,
phrases.notes: Someone who also heard these rulings

phrases.english: and I did not find one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַרְתִּי עַל כׇּל תַּלְמִידָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of reports by noting that none of them were confirmed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three rulings are a tradition from a single student, with no second witness.

steps.title: What does the word 'furthermore' refer back to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which earlier teaching the word ״וְעוֹד״ in the משנה continues.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What was taught before, that the משנה says "and furthermore"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a question about wording. The word ״וְעוֹד״ means something came before it, so the גמרא asks what that was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְעוֹד״ ("and furthermore") suggests the משנה is adding to an earlier teaching of the same kind. The גמרא wants to identify exactly what is being added to. This question sets up the attempts to answer it that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: The discussion of the משנה begins

phrases.english: What was taught, that it teaches "and furthermore"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי ״וְעוֹד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה text to the גמרא's analysis of its wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier teaching the word ״וְעוֹד״ continues.

steps.title: First suggestion: one stringency followed by another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that ״וְעוֹד״ is used because the תנא taught one stringency and now adds a second.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because he taught one stringency and then teaches another, and that is why it says "and furthermore"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, using the word אילימא ("if you say"). This tells you the answer is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the earlier teaching was strict, about the boards around a well. The new teaching is also strict. Two strict rulings in a row would explain the word "furthermore."

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: אילימא almost always introduces an answer the גמרא will reject. Do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּתְנָא לֵיהּ חֲדָא לְחוּמְרָא
phrases.english: If you say it is because he taught one stringency
and then teaches another,
for that reason it teaches "and furthermore" —

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּתְנָא לֵיהּ חֲדָא לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question about ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״וְעוֹד״ appears because a second stringency follows a first one.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה also taught two stringencies without 'furthermore'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבי יהודה also taught one stringency and then another, yet the משנה did not say ״וְעוֹד״ for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהודה taught one stringency and then taught another, and the משנה does not say "and furthermore"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just offered by pointing to a case that does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two stringencies in a row were enough to cause the word ״וְעוֹד״, it should also appear with רבי יהודה. It does not. So the suggested reason cannot be correct.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehuda —
he taught one stringency
and teaches another,
and it does not teach "and furthermore"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דִּתְנָא לֵיהּ חֲדָא לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in step 16 with a case that contradicts it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that a second stringency is what causes the word ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same pattern appears with רבי יהודה, yet the משנה does not say ״וְעוֹד״ there. So the pattern does not explain the word.

steps.title: The difference: the חכמים interrupted there, but not here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 17. With רבי יהודה, the חכמים broke in between his statements. With רבי יהודה בן בבא, nobody broke in, so the משנה can say ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the חכמים interrupted him. Here, the חכמים did not interrupt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its suggestion about ״וְעוֹד״. It explains why רבי יהודה's second stringency did not get the word ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבי יהודה, the חכמים argued with him in the middle, so his two statements were not back to back. With רבי יהודה בן בבא, his two statements come one right after the other. The word ״וְעוֹד״ ("and furthermore") only fits when the second statement directly follows the first.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (our case, רבי יהודה בן בבא)
The Rabbis interrupted him (broke in to argue)

phrases.english: There, the Rabbis interrupted him;
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יהודה, whose statements were broken up by the חכמים' disagreement.

phrases.english: here, the Rabbis did not interrupt him.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה בן בבא's two rulings follow each other directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם אַפְסְקוּהּ רַבָּנַן, הָכָא לָא אַפְסְקוּהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by pointing out a difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any second stringency from the same תנא should be introduced with ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְעוֹד״ is only used when the תנא's two statements were not interrupted by the חכמים.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי אליעזר in מסכת סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new rule. In מסכת סוכה, the חכמים interrupted רבי אליעזר, yet the משנה still says ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that wherever the חכמים interrupted, the משנה does not say ״וְעוֹד״? But look at רבי אליעזר in מסכת סוכה: the חכמים interrupted him, and the משנה still says ״וְעוֹד״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It brings a case where there was an interruption and the word ״וְעוֹד״ is still used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said an interruption by the חכמים prevents the use of ״וְעוֹד״. But in מסכת סוכה, רבי אליעזר gave a ruling, the חכמים argued, and then the משנה says ״וְעוֹד אָמַר רבי אליעזר״. So an interruption alone cannot be the reason.

phrases.english: And wherever the Rabbis interrupted him,
phrases.notes: Testing the rule from step 18.

phrases.english: does the משנה not teach "and furthermore"?
But there is רבי אליעזר in מסכת סוכה,
phrases.notes: In סוכה 27a, רבי אליעזר requires 14 meals in the סוכה, the חכמים disagree, and then the משנה goes on with another ruling of his.

phrases.english: where the Rabbis interrupted him, and yet it teaches "and furthermore"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּאַפְסְקוּהּ רַבָּנַן לָא קָתָנֵי ״וְעוֹד״? וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction just made in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 18 that an interruption by the חכמים prevents the משנה from saying ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: in מסכת סוכה there was an interruption, and ״וְעוֹד״ is still used.

steps.title: Same-topic interruption versus different-topic interruption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens its answer. In מסכת סוכה, the חכמים interrupted on רבי אליעזר's own topic. With רבי יהודה, they interrupted on a different matter, which breaks the link.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they interrupted him on his own subject. Here, they interrupted him on a different subject.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from מסכת סוכה by refining its rule about interruptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the חכמים argue on the same topic, the discussion stays about the תנא's own words, so ״וְעוֹד״ still connects back to him. When the interruption is about something else entirely, his first statement is far away and forgotten, so ״וְעוֹד״ no longer fits.
steps.whatToRemember: The word ״וְעוֹד״ is used when a תנא's second ruling directly continues his first. An argument on the same topic does not break that link; an argument on a different topic does.

phrases.english: There, it was on his own topic that they interrupted him.
phrases.notes: In סוכה, the חכמים argued about the same law of סוכה meals.

phrases.english: Here, they interrupted him on a different matter.
phrases.notes: With רבי יהודה, the interruption was on another subject, so the link to his first statement was cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, בְּמִילְּתֵיהּ הוּא דְּאַפְסְקוּהּ. הָכָא, בְּמִילְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי אַפְסְקוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by refining the distinction of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any interruption at all by the חכמים would prevent the use of ״וְעוֹד״.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an interruption on a different topic breaks the link; an interruption on the same topic still allows ״וְעוֹד״.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: one may carry even without any sign of living there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. רבי עקיבא says one may carry inside the enclosure even if it has none of the signs of living there that the others required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Even if it has none of these things, one may carry inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on and quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up a new discussion about רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinions said an enclosure of about seventy אמות and a bit needs a sign of living there, like a watchman's hut or a house, to allow carrying. רבי עקיבא is more lenient: as long as the size fits, no such sign is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who gives the lenient view here
Even if it does not have

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ
phrases.english: Even if it has none of all these,
phrases.notes: "These" means the signs that someone lives there, like a watchman's hut, a house or a pit, mentioned earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: one may carry inside it.
phrases.notes: As long as it is no larger than seventy אמות and a bit by seventy אמות and a bit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ מְטַלְטְלִין בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ״וְעוֹד״ discussion and opens a new topic by quoting the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, carrying is allowed in an enclosure up to seventy אמות and a bit square even without any sign of living there.
